note: The 17 lesser issues from AUDIT-2026-10-04.md. Four operation types: 'set' changes fields on an existing row, 'add' appends a new allowance row, 'recode' renames a row's code and resets its fields, 'drop_field' removes a field. Reversible via apply-lesser.py --revert. Two of the original 17 findings were my error: British Airways and Turkish Airlines already held the correct published personal item in their bundled rows. The audit's compact dump filtered '__' rows, so I read them as missing. BA is no issue at all; Turkish needed only its 4 kg limit recorded. Scoot's 'no_carry_on' and flydubai's 'lite_bag' turned out to be genuine fare rows holding wrong boxes rather than spurious duplicates, so both became 'set' ops. flydubai's is a wrong measurement in its own right: the Economy Lite row held the standard cabin bag's dimensions, telling Lite passengers they could bring a full cabin bag.
